items.q: How does Kelly Starrett define mobility?
items.a: Not foam-rolling culture or "bendy before big." Mobility = **access to normative range of motion** — the ranges **every physical therapist expects** — **without a 45-minute prep ritual** or 27 supplements first.

items.q: What restores ranges faster than stretch marathons?
items.a: **Exposure at low load**. Sitting shrinks the movement options your brain considers safe. First-order fix: get the human **exposed to the shapes** you're trying to restore — not endless passive stretching.

items.q: What evening habit rebuilds hip and floor positions?
items.a: **20–30 minutes of evening floor sitting** — cross-legged, long sit, 90/90, squat — and **fidget freely**. The brain re-learns shapes it never sees in chairs.

items.q: How is a movement diet different from the gym hour?
items.a: Separate **daily movement minimums** from the **1-hour gym block**. Fitness can happen in **10 minutes** — Juliet's **"10 at 10"** air squats/kettlebell swings/pull-ups at 10 PM when parenting/business peak.

items.q: Is there one perfect desk posture?
items.a: No. Use a **varied workstation**: stand, sit, stool without back support, kickstand fidget. **No single static ideal** — vary positions all day.

items.q: Should you foam roll on the ground before training or a fight?
items.a: *"Do not lay on the ground and foam roll… That is the worst way to get ready for a fight ever."* Replace ground rolling with **5–10 min of play**: medicine ball, mini trampoline, barbell complexes, **rope flow**, breath-hold — and add **speed/velocity** missing from most warmups.

items.q: What low-rep warmup does Poliquin-style strength continuity use?
items.a: One **~8-rep first set** to remind the brain — not a **15→10→8** pyramid. Supports **decades-long strength continuity** instead of high-rep ramps that don't transfer.

items.q: What simple screen exposes global ROM restrictions?
items.a: The **overhead squat**: bar overhead, squat — exposes **ankle, hip, and T-spine** limits simply. Pair with the **couch stretch** (knee in wall corner) to test **hip extension / anterior chain** after sitting.

items.q: How do you know a mobilization is too deep?
items.a: *"If I'm mobilizing you and you suddenly stop breathing, you're going too deep."* Breath is the **depth gauge**; you need **volitional contraction control**. Morning **8–10 min spin-up**: pick hip (back/knee), shoulder (neck/shoulder), or breath.

items.q: Why isn't "swelling" only about sprained ankles?
items.a: Airplane **cankles** and chronic joint puffiness are **congested tissue**. **Muscle contraction drives lymphatic drainage**; decongested tissues **heal faster and hurt less**. Fascia + skeleton + muscle + nervous system work as **one system**.

items.q: Why question the default RICE ice reflex?
items.a: Cold/ice may **suppress prostaglandin signaling** and **stem-cell homing** to damaged tissue — you may need those chemical signalers. Also use **incident vs injury** language: reserve "injury" for clear mechanical trauma (bone-out); call tweaks **incidents** to avoid catastrophizing.
